### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Journal's own Guide for Authors page (sciencedirect.com/journal/child-abuse-and-neglect/publish/guide-for-authors, confirmed via search snippet, direct fetch 403'd) explicitly points authors to Elsevier's group-wide generative-AI policy rather than stating a journal-specific one. Elsevier policy: AI tools may be used for literature synthesis, structuring, language polishing, and figure/data-visualization generation, but never as a substitute for human judgment; use must be disclosed in a declaration statement (exemptions: grammar/spell-check, reference managers, accessibility tech); AI cannot be listed as author; authors remain fully accountable and must vet the AI tool's data-privacy/training terms before use. Moderate, disclosure-gated policy -- not a ban, not fully open, hence 3/5. Leniency and gate are inherited from the Elsevier-wide policy, not journal-specific customization. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/generative-ai-policies-for-journals |
